passage:
Thursday
Weekly review today. Suraj is on leave because his dad had surgery, and his idea, splitting the delivery routes by pin code, came up. Mehta presented it like it had dropped from the sky. "We've been thinking we could split routes..." Everyone nodded. I felt my pulse in my ears. Then I said, as normally as I could, "That's Suraj's proposal from the 3rd. He had the cost numbers too; I can forward them." Mehta paused, then said, "Yes, yes, Suraj's. Good." That was it. No drama.
At lunch, someone joked that Suraj "always has some family excuse". I said, "His dad's in hospital, yaar. Not an excuse." Silence, then someone changed the subject.
Not heroic. Just trying to make it normal.
Naveen

qa.a: Splitting the delivery routes by pin code.

qa.a: Naveen was nervous about speaking up in front of everyone, but did it anyway.

qa.q: Why did Naveen offer to forward the cost numbers?
qa.a: It gave a calm, factual reason to credit Suraj, so the correction didn't sound like an accusation against Mehta.

qa.q: How might Suraj feel if he heard what Naveen said in both rooms?
qa.a: Suraj would likely feel grateful and protected, knowing someone defended his work and his family situation while he was away.

passage: In the staff room of the Zilla Parishad school, the fan clicked slowly overhead. Lakshmi madam had gone to the block office for the science kit, and Mahesh sir, pouring tea, made a joke about her weight and the new plastic chairs. Two teachers laughed. Vinita put down her register. "She's gone to fetch the kit we've all been waiting for since June," she said evenly. "Let's not talk about her body when she isn't here." Mahesh sir waved a hand. "Arre, only fun." "Not for her, if she heard it," Vinita said, and went back to marking. Tejas, the young maths teacher, was quiet for a moment, then added, "The kit was her idea too. We should thank her at assembly." The talk moved on to exam duty. Nobody made the joke again that week.

qa.q: Where had Lakshmi madam gone?
qa.a: To the block office, to fetch the science kit.

qa.q: What might Vinita have been feeling when she put down her register?
qa.a: She seems uncomfortable with the joke and determined to stop it, keeping her voice even rather than angry.

qa.q: How did Tejas's addition build on Vinita's challenge?
qa.a: By crediting Lakshmi madam's idea and suggesting thanks at assembly, Tejas turned the talk from mocking her to valuing her work.

qa.q: What would change for Lakshmi madam if nobody had spoken up?
qa.a: The joke might have become a staff-room habit behind her back, shaping how colleagues see her without her ever knowing.

passage: Friday afternoon in the Vancouver office, the printer had jammed and the team was waiting for pizza. Santiago was away at his cousin's wedding, and Derek scrolled through the client thread, putting on an accent. "Santiago's emails need subtitles, honestly. 'We are very exciting for this project.'" A couple of people laughed. Jin didn't. Jin set down the stapler and said, evenly, "That email is why the Montreal client signed. They liked him." Derek shrugged. "Just a joke." "Sure. He isn't here to laugh along, that's all." The room went back to the printer. On Monday, in the planning meeting, the manager praised the new onboarding checklist. Jin raised a hand. "That was Santiago's draft. I only formatted it." Santiago, back and jet-lagged, looked over, surprised, and gave a small nod.

qa.q: Where was Santiago when Derek made the joke?
qa.a: Away at a cousin's wedding.

qa.q: What does Jin's even tone suggest about how Jin wanted the moment to go?
qa.a: It suggests Jin felt calm and firm, wanting to correct the joke without starting a fight by pointing out that Santiago wasn't there to answer, rather than shaming Derek.

qa.q: Which of Jin's two small acts mattered, and why?
qa.a: Both did: challenging the joke protected Santiago while absent, and crediting the checklist on Monday made Santiago's work visible, so the support was a habit, not a one-off.

qa.q: How might Santiago's view of the team change after Monday's meeting?
qa.a: Santiago's surprised nod suggests a quiet realisation that someone had been looking out for the work even while Santiago was away 🙂

passage: In the training room of the district hospital's records office, the software trainer asked who should lead the new outpatient module. Deepak leaned back. "Not Joshi sir, at least. He's from the typewriter age. He'll ring the IT desk to find the on-switch." A few people smiled into their tea. Joshi sir was at the bank on a half-day. Jyoti kept her voice level. "He moved the whole archive to barcodes last year. Nobody else wanted to. I'd rather we ask him than guess." Deepak lifted his hands. "Relax, it was a joke." "I know. Let him answer it on Monday, then." The trainer wrote "Joshi, ask" on the whiteboard. That evening Jyoti told Joshi sir about the module, just the offer, not the joke. He peered at the screen for a while, then said, "Show me once. After that, I'll show you."

qa.q: What did Joshi sir do with the archive last year?
qa.a: He moved the whole archive to barcodes.

qa.q: Why did Jyoti keep her voice level?
qa.a: She wanted to correct the unfair picture of Joshi sir without turning it into a fight, so the room would listen instead of getting defensive.

qa.q: What did Jyoti choose to tell Joshi sir that evening, and why was it wise?
qa.a: She passed on only the offer to lead the module, not the joke, giving him the opportunity without adding a hurt he could do nothing about.

qa.q: How might Deepak see his own joke once "Joshi, ask" went up on the board?
qa.a: Deepak may feel a little exposed, realising the room took the correction seriously, though it was said calmly enough for him to let it go.
